lots.title: Inspection & Maintenance of Indoor Gymnasium, Fitness & Sport Equipment and Outdoor Schools Play & Sport Equipment
lots.description: Single-lot ESPO framework call-off (framework ref 107_26). Subject matter is the inspection and maintenance of indoor gymnasium, fitness and sport equipment and outdoor schools' play and sport equipment, delivered to Contracting Authorities under the ESPO Framework Agreement. This source document is the Form of Contract / Call-Off Terms template (Framework Schedule 3); it defines the legal and performance envelope rather than enumerating product-level specifications.
requirements: Supplier shall supply the Goods and/or Services during the Contract Period in accordance with the Customer's requirements as set out in the Contract (clause 6.1.1).

Supplier shall at all times comply with the Technical Standards and Quality Standards and, where applicable, maintain accreditation with the relevant Technical Standards and Quality Standards authorisation body (clause 6.3.1).

Supplier shall perform its obligations in accordance with the Law and Good Industry Practice; where a standard has not been specified in the Contract, the Supplier shall agree the relevant standard with the Customer before supply commences (clause 6.3.1).
Goods shall be free from defects in design and workmanship, fit for purpose, and supplied in accordance with the Supplier Solution and Specification (clauses 6.3.5.1 – 6.3.5.2).
Delivery shall meet the requirements stated in the Master Contract Schedule/ITT Response and proceed in accordance with the Implementation Plan and Milestones (clauses 6.4.1 – 6.4.2).

Supplier shall meet or exceed the Service Levels set out in Schedule 1 Part A; Service Credits apply for Service Failures and a Critical Service Failure gives the Customer a right to terminate (clauses 11.1 and Schedule 1).
Supplier shall maintain business continuity arrangements throughout the Contract Period so that delivery of the Goods and/or Services is subject to minimum disruption (clause 8.1).
Supplier shall implement measurement and monitoring tools sufficient to report on performance against the Service Levels (clause 11.2).

Where the Goods/Services require Staff to work in Regulated Activity with children and/or vulnerable adults, the Supplier shall make enhanced DBS checks including appropriate barred-list checks and comply with the Safeguarding of Vulnerable Groups Act 2006 (clauses 15.7 – 15.11).

Supplier shall comply with the Customer's environmental policy, maintain a suitable environmental management system, and minimise GHG emissions and other pollutants in performing the Contract (clauses 26.1 – 26.4).
Supplier shall keep and maintain full and accurate records of the operation of the Contract, including supply-chain traceability, for the Contract Period plus six (6) Years (clause 28.1).

evaluation_criteria.criterion: Service Level compliance (post-award performance gate, not tender award)
evaluation_criteria.summary: Schedule 1 Part A defines that Service Credits are calculated as (100% minus % of Service Level achieved) of the Contract Charges; repeated or critical failure of agreed Service Levels is the trigger for remedies including termination. The table of specific Service Levels is left as a Customer drafting note ("Insert the appropriate Service Levels above") and is not populated in the template, so no scored evaluation criteria are extractable from this document.

technical_standards.standard_ref: BSI British Standards / ISO (by reference via 'Quality Standards' definition)
technical_standards.context: The 'Quality Standards' definition in clause 3.1 refers to standards published by BSI British Standards (National Standards Body of the UK), the International Organisation for Standardisation, and other reputable bodies that a skilled operator would reasonably be expected to comply with. This is a normative reference to families of standards rather than a specific standard number.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: "Quality Standards" means the quality standards published by BSI British Standards, the National Standards Body of the United Kingdom, the International Organisation for Standardisation or other reputable or equivalent body

technical_standards.standard_ref: Good Industry Practice (governing standard of performance)
technical_standards.context: Clause 3.1 defines Good Industry Practice as the skill and care reasonably expected from a skilled and experienced person in the relevant sector, and clause 6.3.1 binds the Supplier to perform in accordance with Law and Good Industry Practice where no specific standard is stated in the Contract.

evidence_anchor.anchor_text: the Supplier shall perform its obligations under this Contract in accordance with the Law and Good Industry Practice

technical_standards.standard_ref: Safeguarding of Vulnerable Groups Act 2006 / DBS enhanced disclosure
technical_standards.context: Clauses 15.7 – 15.11 impose statutory safeguarding obligations: enhanced Disclosure & Barring Service checks (including children's barred list where applicable) for Staff engaged in Regulated Activity with children or vulnerable adults, with re-checks at least every three years. Relevant for school-premises inspection/maintenance delivery.

technical_standards.context: Clause 13.2.2 requires supplier invoices to comply with the standard and syntaxes published in the UK version of Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2017/1870. This is an operational compliance standard rather than a goods-level technical standard.

warnings.message: Document is a framework call-off contract template (FRAMEWORK SCHEDULE 3 – FORM OF CONTRACT AND CALL-OFF TERMS, contract ref 107_26) rather than a tender specification or statement of requirements. It defines the legal and performance envelope for the Goods/Services but contains no scored award criteria, no product-level specifications, and no populated technical-standard numbers. Lot-level output was seeded from the document title block and notice context; per-specification product requirements are not extractable.

The document does not enumerate individual product specifications, quantities, or candidate names. All Master Contract Schedule cells intended to hold concrete product/service details (e.g. Customer's equipment, Technical Standards, Quality Standards, Specification) are blank placeholders accompanied by Customer Drafting Notes. No product_requirement_seeds were emitted for this reason.
